messages:
jen (Customer): Hey team — after the scheduled cert rotation at 02:00 UTC, our services in the private VPC started failing TLS validation when calling Redwood endpoints. ~30% of requests now return connection errors and our app logs show: `verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate`. Public requests (from our office IP) to the same host succeed. Can you help?

emily (Support): Sorry you're hitting this. Quick ones: which deployment (Dedicated/Private)? URL you hit (masked ok). Do you have a curl / openssl snippet?

jen (Customer): This is Private (VPC). Endpoint: api.internal.example (we'll mask). Sample from a failing host:  
```
$ curl -v https://api.internal.example/v1/health
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Newsession Ticket (0x23)
* error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert certificate unknown
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
```
I also ran openssl:  
```
$ openssl s_client -showcerts -connect api.internal.example:443 -servername api.internal.example
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = api.internal.example
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.internal.example
   i:/CN=redwood-intermediate
---
```
It only prints the leaf, no intermediate in the chain. We uploaded the bundle via the Console during rotation.

emily (Support): Thanks. Two quick hypotheses: 1) uploaded bundle was missing/reordered intermediate, or 2) OCSP/responder egress is blocked so stapling is timing out in some client paths and causing verification fallout.

raj (SRE): Looking at our rotator logs around 02:00 UTC: 
```
2026-02-18T02:00:12Z cert-rotator: upload received, size=3240 bytes
2026-02-18T02:00:12Z cert-rotator: bundle parsed, order=ROOT,INTERMEDIATE,LEAF
2026-02-18T02:00:12Z cert-rotator: stored bundle id=cb-12345
2026-02-18T02:00:12Z cert-rotator: applied to private endpoint, trigger reload
```
That order is root-first which some proxies (haproxy/nginx) will drop the intermediate on reload if chain order isn't leaf->intermediate->root. The rotator should normally enforce leaf-first, but I see the parser logged root-first. We'll re-run a normalization job.

marco (Infra): Also, we saw multiple TCP resets from customer VPC to our OCSP responder IPs during the same window. Can you confirm whether your egress allowlist/proxy rewrites ocsp responder hostnames?

jen (Customer): Interesting — we do have a split-horizon DNS setup for some external domains (corporate internal overrides). I just tried: 
```
$ dig +short ocsp.letsencrypt.org
10.1.5.8
```
That internal IP is not reachable to the public responder and our proxy blocks direct egress to the public internet for that host. We also see logs of outbound resets to the OCSP IP.

emily (Support): Aha — that fits. If the client's TLS stack requests stapled OCSP or the server tries to fetch OCSP/responder during rotation tooling, a DNS rewrite to an internal IP will cause timeouts/resets and can result in clients failing verification or proxies trimming the chain. Two-pronged: we need the correct bundle order and you need to allow OCSP/CRL/HTTP(s) egress to the actual responders (or ensure your split-horizon points to a reachable responder).

jen (Customer): What immediate steps should we take? We can update egress rules but that'll take ops change control for a few hours.

raj (SRE): Short-term mitigations: 
- Re-upload a normalized chain (leaf -> intermediate -> root) so proxies don't drop the intermediate on reload. We can do that from our side now.
- If you can, temporarily allow egress to OCSP/CRL responder FQDNs (e.g., ocsp.letsencrypt.org, crl.example-ca.com) or allow HTTP/443 to the responder IPs.
- If egress change is blocked, as a temporary workaround, we can enable a non-stapling mode on the edge for your private endpoint (serve full chain without requiring OCSP fetch). This reduces revocation checking but restores traffic while you sort DNS/egress.

cert-rotator-bot: Received re-normalize request for bundle cb-12345, creating cb-12345-v2 with order leaf,intermediate,root. Applying to endpoint api.internal.example...

cert-rotator-bot: Applied cb-12345-v2 successfully, reload triggered (haproxy).

marco (Infra): After the reapply, haproxy reload logs show the full chain was preserved. I also pushed a small change to ensure uploaded bundles are auto-normalized on ingest.

jen (Customer): After re-upload, we're seeing success on a few hosts, but some still fail. I ran the openssl command again from a failing host and now it shows the intermediate present. However our app still errors intermittently. Sample app log: `tls: certificate signed by unknown authority`.

emily (Support): That intermittent bit matches the split-horizon ocsp/DNS angle — some hosts resolve ocsp responder to internal IP and others to public (depending on which resolver/cache they hit). Please run a curl to ocsp responder from both a failing and a working host: 
```
$ curl -v https://ocsp.letsencrypt.org/ -I --connect-timeout 5
```
If it times out or resets on failing hosts then egress/DNS still the culprit.

jen (Customer): Confirmed: failing host -> connection reset to ocsp.letsencrypt.org; working host -> 200 OK. Our ops will open a narrow egress path to the OCSP/CRL responders (change approved).

raj (SRE): Great. Next steps: 
- ops opens egress to OCSP/CRL responders (or remove split-horizon override for those FQDNs).
- we'll keep the normalized bundle active and monitor.
- postmortem: we'll add a validation step in rotator to reject root-first bundles and add a check that fetching OCSP/CRL endpoints from within a sample VPC isn't failing due to DNS overrides (warn on split-horizon).

jen (Customer): Thanks all. One ask: can you add a short KB we can reference for future rotations (what ports/hosts to allow, recommended bundle format)?

emily (Support): On it — I'll draft a KB and paste here. High level: 
- Bundle order: leaf -> intermediate(s) -> root (root optional but last if present). Ensure trailing newline at EOF.
- Egress allowlist: OCSP responders (port 80/443 depending on CA), CRL distribution points (HTTP), and the rotator service IPs for uploads. Example FQDNs: ocsp.letsencrypt.org, ocsp.identrust.com, crl3.digicert.com.
- Troubleshooting commands: 
  - `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect HOST:443 -servername HOST` to view chain; 
  - `curl -v https://ocsp.example -I` to check OCSP reachability; 
  - `dig +short <ocsp-host>` to confirm DNS resolution.

marco (Infra): I'll include notes about split-horizon DNS pitfalls in the KB draft.

jen (Customer): Egress is opened now. I can confirm all hosts are healthy after a minute. Thanks to the team for the fast turnaround, and the KB will be helpful. :thumbsup:

emily (Support): Glad to hear it. We'll keep monitoring for the next hour and follow up with the PM to add the rotator validation. Closing loop once the KB and validation are live. :white_check_mark:
